package_info.why_malicious: The API implementation allowed unauthorized access and modification of user preferences, including sensitive metadata, due to missing or broken object-level authorization (BOLA). This enabled both data leakage and manipulation by anonymous or unauthorized users, violating user privacy and data integrity.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request to API endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the API endpoint allows any user (including anonymous) to retrieve arbitrary user preferences and metadata by specifying a user ID and preference type, resulting in unauthorized data exposure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The endpoint exposes user-specific data to any requester without authentication or authorization checks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict access to user preferences to the authenticated user or authorized parties only. Here, any user can access any other user's data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be an authenticated user retrieving their own preferences.
key_indicators: User ID is directly specifiable in the URL
Sensitive metadata (activity timestamps, course IDs) exposed

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP PUT request to API endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the API endpoint allows any user (including anonymous) to modify arbitrary user preferences and metadata by specifying a user ID and preference type, resulting in unauthorized data manipulation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The endpoint allows modification of another user's data without authentication or authorization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict modification of user preferences to the authenticated user or authorized parties only. Here, any user can alter any other user's data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be an authenticated user updating their own preferences.
key_indicators: User ID is directly specifiable in the URL
Ability to arbitrarily set or overwrite user data

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a GET request to the userPreferences API endpoint with a target user ID and preference type to enumerate or exfiltrate user preference data and metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive user data (privacy violation).

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a PUT request to the same API endpoint with a crafted payload to overwrite or manipulate the target user's preferences and activity metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can bias user experience, manipulate recommendations, or further exploit the platform.

behavioral_signatures: API requests to userPreferences endpoints with user IDs not matching the authenticated user
Anonymous or unauthenticated requests to sensitive user data endpoints
Unusual frequency or volume of GET/PUT requests to userPreferences API
network_indicators: Unusual or unauthenticated traffic to www.coursera.org/api/userPreferences.v1/*
PUT requests to userPreferences API from non-logged-in sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor API logs for requests to /api/userPreferences.v1/ where the user ID in the path does not match the authenticated session user, or where requests are made without authentication. Flag and alert on any PUT or GET requests to this endpoint from anonymous users or from users accessing IDs other than their own. Rate-limit and review bulk access patterns to this endpoint.
